content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Text Summarization (Extractive and Abstractive) in Natural Language Processing"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Text summarization is a core task in Natural Language Processing (NLP) aimed at creating a concise and fluent summary of a longer text document while preserving its key information. There are two primary paradigms for text summarization: Extractive and Abstractive."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Extractive Summarization"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Extractive summarization works by selecting the most important sentences, phrases, or paragraphs directly from the original source text and concatenating them. Because the words are pulled verbatim, the output maintains grammatical correctness and factual accuracy from the source."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Pros: Simple to implement, computationally efficient, and generally avoids factual hallucinations."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Cons: Lacks human-like phrasing, cannot synthesize new sentences, and summaries can feel disjointed."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Abstractive Summarization"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"Abstractive summarization uses advanced deep learning architectures to understand the underlying semantics of the text and generate novel sentences. This mimics how humans summarize documents, often utilizing paraphrasing, reordering, and new vocabulary."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Pros: Produces fluent, human-like, and concise summaries that can synthesize information from multiple parts of the text."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Cons: Computationally expensive, requires large datasets, and is prone to factual hallucinations."},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Implementation Example: Abstractive Summarization using Hugging Face Transformers"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"The following Python code demonstrates how to implement an abstractive text summarization pipeline utilizing a pre-trained Transformer model (BART) from the Hugging Face library."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"from transformers import pipeline\\n\\n# Initialize the summarization pipeline with a pre-trained model\\nsummarizer = pipeline(\"summarization\", model=\"facebook/bart-large-cnn\")\\n\\n# Define the source text to summarize\\ntext = \"Natural Language Processing (NLP) is a subfield of artificial intelligence, computer science, and linguistics focused on the interactions between computers and human language. It is used to apply machine learning algorithms to text and speech. Over recent years, transformer-based architectures like BERT, GPT, and BART have revolutionized the field by enabling models to capture deep contextual representations of language.\"\\n\\n# Generate the abstractive summary\\nsummary = summarizer(text, max_length=60, min_length=20, do_sample=False)\\n\\nprint(\"Generated Summary:\", summary[0]['summary_text'])"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Both extractive and abstractive summarization techniques have their own use cases. Extractive methods are reliable when factual consistency is strictly required, whereas abstractive methods excel in generating human-like, condensed narratives for content consumption."}]
